Q: Make Parallelogram in react native A:

This was a painful realization, but it does work when using SVG's ( since react-native-svg exists ).

A bit of a pain to implement it if they all need to look different in your case, but it is still a somewhat viable workaround.

Q: Export translate() and connect(mapStateToProps) from the same react-native file A:

This is where a compose-function comes in handy, instead of doing something like:

export default translate(connect(mapStateToProps))(entryPage)

You can simply do:

export default compose(translate, connect(mapStateToProps))(entryPage)

Here is a compose-function published on NPM, there are also compose-functions bundled in many popular libraries like Ramda, Recompose or Redux.

Q: JPackage app-image exe launches multiple exe's in JDK 17+ A:

This behavior is not related to Swing — it started with JDK 17 because jpackage changed how Windows app‑images launch executables. Each .exe now relaunches itself with a modified java.library.path, which is why you see two processes in Task Manager.

References:

  • JDK-8301247 — JPackage app-image exe launches multiple exe's in JDK 17+

  • JDK-8340311 — similar issue reported for JDK 22+

Workarounds:

  1. Use win.norestart=true (JDK 24+) After generating the app‑image, edit the .cfg file in /app/<app_name>.cfg and add:

    Code

    [Application]
win.norestart=true

    This prevents the double EXE launch.

  2. Explicitly set java.library.path If your app depends on native libraries, set the path in java-options instead of relying on the duplicated process:

    Code

    java-options=-Djava.library.path=${windir}\System32;$APPDIR\yourlibfolder

  3. Fallback to older jpackage executable If you are building your own installer from the app‑image, you can replace the generated .exe with one built using JDK 16 or earlier. Rename it appropriately before bundling.

Summary: This is a known regression in JDK 17+. The cleanest fix is to use win.norestart=true in the config (available JDK 24+). For earlier JDKs, either patch the .cfg manually or swap in an older jpackage launcher.

Q: Typescript Import does "not import types" A:

In ESLint, "Unsafe construction of ... typed value" can indicate that you're assigning a value an any type. While this is legal in TypeScript, it's not recommended (as otherwise you might as well just use JavaScript) so the linter will give you a warning/error (depending on your severity setting).

Try explicitly typing x. I.e.

const x: PrismaPg = new PrismaPg({});

Q: How to resolve error 'Class attribute on column 1 of different items do not match' in R A:

The dput you provided for dt.tidied[[142]] was incomplete so I will explain what could be happening with an example. Let's assume your d1 and d2 data.tables look like this:

library(lubridate)

d1 = structure(
  list(V1 = c(NA, NA, NA),
       V2 = c("SRad(SRAD)","Temp [?C] (TT)", "Temp QCode (TTC)")),
  row.names = c(NA, -3L),
  class = c("data.table", "data.frame")
)

d2 = structure(
  list(V1 = c(NA, NA, NA),
       V2 = c(956.902, 961.01, 965.114)),
  row.names = c(NA, -44615L),
  class = c("data.table", "data.frame")
)

We'll make a list to hold these two data.tables and store them in element 1 and 2 of the list:

dt.tidied.working <- vector("list", length = 2)

dt.tidied.working[[1]] <- d1
dt.tidied.working[[2]] <- d2

Now we can check the class attribute of the column 1 for each list element:

> class(dt.tidied.working[[1]]$V1)
[1] "logical"

> class(dt.tidied.working[[2]]$V1)
[1] "logical"

So we can see that in this very simple example that both columns have the same class, logical, so when we use rbindlist we won't get the error you're getting.

merged <- rbindlist(dt.tidied.working, fill = TRUE, use.names = TRUE)

 V1               V2
1: NA       SRad(SRAD)
2: NA   Temp [?C] (TT)
3: NA Temp QCode (TTC)
4: NA          956.902
5: NA           961.01
6: NA          965.114

Now let's change the class attribute for the second data.table to what I think your full data.table might contain based on your comments so far:

## not working example
d1 = structure(
  list(V1 = c(NA, NA, NA),
       V2 = c("SRad(SRAD)","Temp [?C] (TT)", "Temp QCode (TTC)")),
  row.names = c(NA, -3L),
  class = c("data.table", "data.frame")
)

d2 = structure(
  list(V1 = ymd_hms(c("2004-08-01T00:00:00","2004-08-02T00:00:00","2004-08-03T00:00:00")),
       V2 = c(956.902, 961.01, 965.114)),
  row.names = c(NA, -44615L),
  class = c("data.table", "data.frame")
)

dt.tidied.not.working <- vector("list", length = 2)

dt.tidied.not.working[[1]] <- d1
dt.tidied.not.working[[2]] <- d2

Now we'll check the class attributes again as in the previous example and you'll see that the two columns now have different attributes and when we try to rbind.list you'll get the same error.

> class(dt.tidied.not.working[[1]]$V1)
[1] "logical"
> class(dt.tidied.not.working[[2]]$V1)
[1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"

> merged <- rbindlist(dt.tidied.not.working, fill = TRUE, use.names = TRUE)
Error in rbindlist(dt.tidied.not.working, fill = TRUE, use.names = TRUE) : 
  Class attribute on column 1 of item 2 does not match with column 1 of item 1.

Potential Solution

Based on your dput of dt.tidied[[23]] it appears that you have NA values where you should have ymd_hms values. This could be the problem you're running into. If that's the case then what you can do is inspect elements of the dt list that contains the files you read in to see which files have NA in column V1. If that is in fact the issue, you will need to figure out what to do with those observations (remove them or fix them by assigning the date/time values).

Also, the d1=dput(dt.tidied[[142]]) output that you provided in your question is incomplete as you did not include structure(... the same way you did for d1=dput(dt.tidied[[23]]). Please provide complete and accurate information as it makes it easier for us to help you.

If you don't want to inspect every single element of your dt list, you can use the rbind.fill function from the plyr library:

library(plyr)

dt.tidied.not.working <- lapply(dt.tidied.not.working, function(x) as.data.frame(x))
merged <- plyr::rbind.fill(dt.tidied.not.working)

> merged
         V1               V2
1        NA       SRad(SRAD)
2        NA   Temp [?C] (TT)
3        NA Temp QCode (TTC)
4 1.091e+09          956.902
5 1.091e+09           961.01
6 1.091e+09          965.114

Q: OAuth "Facebook Platform" "invalid_request" "Application does not have permission for this action - /ads_archive with system user token A:

Using Facebook Login For Business to invoke the user dialog and trade the returned login code for a user access token worked.

https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/facebook-login-for-business#invoke-a-login-dialog

From my testing it appears that the system user access token doesn't work with the Ad Library API.

It also appears that without an App Role assigned on the app itself to your user, the user access won't work and will show an error like so:

{
  "error": {
    "message": "Application does not have permission for this action",
    "type": "OAuthException",
    "code": 10,
    "error_subcode": 2332004,
    "is_transient": false,
    "error_user_title": "App role required",
    "error_user_msg": "You need to be assigned a role by the app owner to continue. Learn more at https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/build-and-test/app-roles",
    "fbtrace_id": "A4Wo90w1V6KRWIJLNILAc4Z"
  }
}

Strange because this means you would have to assign a user a role each time to use this api and you would have to add each user to the meta app itself. Since you can't add test users, this means you would have to add developer users, which defeats the purpose of having a public api.
